title: [D5 Tools] Disclosure recording and send policy
summary: `helena.disclosure` is the two halves of `concept/07`'s privacy sentence: `SendPolicy` is a per-source whitelist loaded from `config/policy.toml` — the host its requests go to, which entity types this deployment permits being disclosed to it, and which fields of the outbound request may be populated — and `Disclosures` is one ledger per agent run holding one typed `Disclosure` per outbound call. `helena.tools.ProviderTool` resolves a permission at construction (so a tool for a source no policy permits cannot be built), enforces it before the cache is read, refuses with a fourth typed reason `send_policy_forbids` rather than trimming, and records the disclosure before the adapter is called. `helena.agents.assess` records a model call on the same footing, once per attempt, because inference is hosted.
assumption_validated: That `concept/07`'s two obligations decompose into one configuration table and one per-run ledger, and that the field half of a send policy can be a property of the code rather than of an adapter's discipline. It can: `SENDABLE_FIELDS` **is** the field set of `helena.tools.ToolCall`, the only object an adapter is handed, so a policy-forbidden field is a request that cannot be assembled and the tenant and the sensor are in no vocabulary at all — a test asserts the two sets equal so a field added to the call cannot become sendable before it is declared. ONE RESULT WAS NEGATIVE AND IS RECORDED AS A DESIGN, NOT AS A FIELD: `cache hit or live` is not on the disclosure row. A row exists only where something was sent, because `concept/07` also says a cache hit discloses nothing and a row saying a run told a provider something it did not is worse than no row; the outcome lives on `RetrievalStep.outcome` on the same assessment, which is what ADR-0017 already said the disclosure record would be derived from, and the two reconcile by a test: provider disclosures == `RunBudget.live_queries_spent`.
makes_buildable: Task 38 (the live adapter) has the host its requests must go to, in policy rather than in code (`send_policy.threatfox.disclosed_to = threatfox-api.abuse.ch`, re-measured 2026-09-09: 401 without the `Auth-Key` header, no credential and no indicator sent), and the guarantee that whatever it builds a body from is the `ToolCall` and nothing else. Task 39 (the analyst loop) builds `Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy())` once beside `RunBudget.of(request)` and threads both through `tool.lookup(..., budget=..., disclosures=...)` and `assess(..., budget=..., disclosures=...)`; `ProviderTool.declaration()` now offers the intersection of what the source covers and what the policy permits, so the loop cannot be handed a tool that invites refusals. Task 41 (replay) gets the counting rule it needs — a run's disclosures are its live queries, and a full replay must therefore record none. Task 42 (orchestration) is the code that owns the ledger: `helena.triage.run` takes it and does not build it. Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets `Disclosures.rows` as the column to store, beside `RunBudget.cost`, and owes both.

verification.detail: 1347 passed in 311.90s, no skips and no failures, engine and broker up (bin/env.sh sourced). 1289 before. New: tests/test_disclosure.py 37 tests (the loader's coverage rules, the record's validation, the ledger, and the sendable-fields-equal-ToolCall-fields assertion), 14 in tests/test_tools.py driving the real dispatch against the migrated engine and the committed ThreatFox extract (including the two the task names), 5 in tests/test_agents.py against the scripted loopback endpoint, 1 in tests/test_triage.py. No new SQL, so nothing new was executed against the engine; the 0017 cache tables the tool tests write to are unchanged. The abuse.ch host in the policy file was verified by one unauthenticated POST that returned 401: no credential and no indicator left this machine, and no value from .env is asserted on or printed anywhere.

escalations.detail: A DISCLOSURE ROW HAS NO CONTRACT FIELD TO LEAVE ON, AND ONE WAS NOT ADDED. `concept/07` and `concept/02` put the record on the *assessment*, not in the agent's answer, and adding a field to `helena.contracts.v1.AgentResult` is an escalation under `concept/instruction.md` §3. The consequence is a shape the next sessions must know: the ledger belongs to the CALLER, which is why `helena.triage.run` takes `disclosures` and does not build one, while it still builds the budget ledger itself (what that becomes leaves on `AgentResult.cost`, which is a contract field). Task 43 should store `Disclosures.rows` as an assessment column, and until it does, a run's disclosure record dies with the process.

NO SOURCE WAS ADDED AND ONE HOST WAS RECORDED. `send_policy.threatfox.disclosed_to` names `threatfox-api.abuse.ch`, which is the host `src/helena/enrichment.py` already recorded from a 2026-09-06 measurement and which I re-measured on 2026-09-09 (401 `{"error": "Unauthorized"}` to an unauthenticated POST). **The query surface behind that host is still unconfirmed** — no per-indicator endpoint appears in the public documentation — and confirming it is task 38's, which may also change whether the analyst tier is `threatfox` or a second source id. What is settled here is only where an analyst-tier query would go, which is what a disclosure record has to name.

THE SEND POLICY IS CHECKED BEFORE THE CACHE IS READ, so a revoked permission stops a source being consulted at all rather than being answered from records fetched while it was in force. The alternative (serve the stored answer, since a hit discloses nothing) is defensible and was rejected: it would let a permission that was withdrawn keep producing claims. Nothing is evicted, so the records stay and a re-permitted source finds them again. Recorded in docs/decisions/0027 §2 with what would reverse it.

invariant_conflicts.detail: The task's step 3 asks for a disclosure row carrying `cache-hit-or-live`, and `concept/07`'s own list names it. A row is written per OUTBOUND CALL and carries no such field, because the same note says a cache hit discloses nothing: a row per retrieval would record a disclosure the run did not make, and a constant `live_query` field on the rows that do exist would be a field with one value. Where the element went is stated in three places rather than dropped — `helena.contracts.v1.RetrievalStep.outcome` on the same assessment, which `docs/decisions/0017` already named as what the disclosure record would be derived from — and the two are made to reconcile by construction and by a test: the count of provider disclosures equals `RunBudget.live_queries_spent`, and `RunBudget.cache_hits` counts the calls that told nobody anything. The stale fallback is the one call in both.

The task's step 3 says 'write a disclosure row' and nothing is written to the store. `concept/instruction.md` §2's 'one store' is not the obstacle — a table in the engine would have been legal — but `concept/02` and `concept/07` both put the record ON THE ASSESSMENT, and no assessment is stored (task 43). A table now would be a second home for a fact the assessment is going to carry, and the project already has the precedent one task old: `helena.budgets.RunBudget` is an in-process ledger that becomes `contract.Cost`, with storage deferred to the same increment. So the rows are typed, ordered, countable and in memory, and the deferral is named in the module docstring, in README and in ADR-0027 §6.

deferred: STORING A DISCLOSURE ROW. The ledger is in-process and ephemeral; `concept/07` allows that of working memory and requires the record on the assessment, which task 43 owes. Until then a run's disclosures are lost when the process ends — the one thing an auditor would actually want.

WHETHER AN INDICATOR THE MODEL INVENTED MAY BE SENT AT ALL. Still the sharpest gap the tool layer leaves, and the send policy does not close it: the policy governs what KINDS of thing and WHICH FIELDS may be sent and never asks where the value came from. Closing it needs the host context beside the tool, which is the analyst runner's shape rather than this layer's. Named in `helena.tools`' 'deliberately not here' section and in ADR-0027 §6.

GOVERNING THE MODEL CHANNEL PER FIELD. What of a context reaches a prompt is the rendering's decision under a recorded `rendering_version`, and a second field list in the send policy would be a second opinion about it. What this increment adds for that channel is the record, not a second gate.

VERIFYING THAT AN ADAPTER SPEAKS TO `disclosed_to`. `helena.tools` holds no URL at all (asserted off its own AST), so the layer could not check the request even in principle. It becomes checkable when a live adapter exists (task 38).
PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from task 36: `[rate_limits]` is read for the live-query derivation and nothing sleeps between calls.
lessons: THE SEND POLICY'S FIELD LIST IS ONLY WORTH ANYTHING IF THE VOCABULARY IS THE REQUEST'S OWN FIELD SET. `SENDABLE_FIELDS` is asserted equal to `tools.ToolCall.model_fields`, so 'a policy-forbidden field cannot reach a request body' is a property of the code rather than a rule an adapter has to remember: the adapter is handed the `ToolCall` and nothing else, so what the policy withholds is a request that cannot be assembled, and the tenant and the sensor are in no vocabulary at all. A field added to the call later fails that test until it is declared here and permitted in the file.

PERMISSION AND CAPABILITY ARE TWO REFUSALS AND COLLAPSING THEM WOULD LOSE THE ACTIONABLE ONE. `entity_type_not_covered` is the source's capability ('a JA3 list has nothing to say about a domain') and is fixed by asking a different source; `send_policy_forbids` is this deployment's permission and is fixed by editing `config/policy.toml`. Same shape as the four ways a call produces no claim, and the loader enforces the containment: a permission wider than the capability is refused at load, because a line permitting something the source cannot answer about is one nothing reads.

A DECLARATION THAT OFFERS WHAT THE DISPATCH WILL REFUSE IS A PROMISE THE LAYER DOES NOT KEEP. `ProviderTool.declaration()` now offers the INTERSECTION of the descriptor's entity types and the policy's, because offering a type every call would be refused for spends a step and a turn of the loop on a refusal the layer could have declined to invite. The model is not told why the set is what it is: a tool description is not where a deployment explains its policy.

RECORD A DISCLOSURE BEFORE THE SEND, NEVER AFTER. A request that reached the provider (or the model endpoint) and then timed out disclosed the indicator anyway, so recording on success under-records exactly the case an operator most needs to see. The cost is a row for a call that failed before it left the process, which over-records in the direction an audit can live with. Both channels do it in that order and both have a test.

A CONFIG KEY IN TOML BELONGS TO THE LAST TABLE THAT WAS OPENED. `send_policy_version` appended at the foot of `config/policy.toml` silently became `rate_limits.send_policy_version` and broke two loaders at once; it lives at the top with the other version keys, with a comment saying why. Cheap to hit and easy to miss, because the file still parses.

THREE LOADERS OVER ONE POLICY FILE NEED THEIR KEY SETS IN ONE PLACE. `helena.policy` owns the path and now names all three sets (`THRESHOLD_KEYS`, `BUDGET_KEYS`, `DISCLOSURE_KEYS`); each loader refuses a key NOTHING reads and none refuses a key another requires, and a test loads the shipped file through all three. Adding a fourth table means adding a set there, not a subtraction in three places.

`disclosed_to` IS A HOST AND THE LOADER REFUSES A URL. `concept/07` requires a credential travelling in a URL to be redacted before anything is logged or stored, and the strongest version of that rule is that the policy file holds no URL to begin with — the tool layer holds none either. `key@host`, a scheme and a path are all refused at load.

MEASURING A HOST IS NOT THE SAME AS CONFIRMING A QUERY SURFACE, AND SAYING SO KEEPS TASK 38 HONEST. One unauthenticated POST to `threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/` returned 401 on 2026-09-09 — that settles WHERE an analyst query would go, which a disclosure record must name, and settles nothing about the request shape, which is what `concept/05` records this project getting wrong repeatedly.

THE DISCLOSURE LEDGER IS THE CALLER'S BECAUSE THE CONTRACT HAS NOWHERE FOR IT. The budget ledger can be built inside `helena.triage.run` because `AgentResult.cost` carries its product out; a disclosure row has no contract field, so a ledger built inside `run` would be a record that dies at the return statement. The asymmetry is the contract's rather than a preference, and it is where the orchestration increment has to own the object.
failed_approaches: Putting `outcome` (`cache_hit` / `live_query`) on the disclosure row so the record would carry `concept/07`'s fifth element literally. Every row a call produces is a live query — a hit writes none — so the field would have had exactly one value, and making it two-valued required moving the write to AFTER the adapter returned, which loses the disclosure of a call that failed mid-flight. Rejected in favour of a reconciliation with the retrieval trace and the live-query budget, argued in ADR-0027 §3.

A `helena_reference_disclosure` table beside the 0017 cache tables. Legal under 'one store' and rejected on the concept's own wording: the record goes on the assessment, no assessment is stored yet, and a table now would compete with the column task 43 has to add.

Widening `SENDABLE_FIELDS` to include `tenant` and `sensor` so the field check would have something interesting to forbid. That is building a hole to prove it can be closed: the layer never puts them in a `ToolCall` and the adapter cannot reach them, so the honest test is that they appear in no request body under any policy — which is what tests/test_tools.py asserts.

Naming the test helper in tests/test_tools.py `record()`. Several tests already bind a local `record`, and the shadowing produced an `UnboundLocalError` in a test that had nothing to do with this increment. It is `disclosures()`.
next_session_should_know: Task 38 is the first live provider tool and this task built the two things that decide what it may send and what gets recorded. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS NOW `ProviderTool(source_id=..., endpoint=..., credential=..., ask=..., cache=..., retention_seconds=..., send_policy=<SendPolicy>, logger=..., redactor=...)` and `tool.lookup(arguments, scope=RunScope.of(request), budget=RunBudget.of(request), disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy()), now=...)`. All four keyword arguments are required and none has a default. `helena.agents.assess` and `helena.triage.run` take `disclosures` on the same terms. (2) A TOOL FOR A SOURCE WITH NO `[send_policy.<source>]` ENTRY CANNOT BE BUILT — `sslbl-ja3` has none, deliberately, because it is a feed the loader copies locally and a local join discloses nothing. An entry means the source may be QUERIED LIVE, which is the same condition `[rate_limits]` states of itself; a live adapter for a new source needs both. (3) THE HOST IS IN POLICY AND NOT IN CODE. `disclosed_to = "threatfox-api.abuse.ch"`, and the loader refuses anything that is not a bare host. `helena.tools` still imports no HTTP machinery and holds no `://` literal, asserted off its own AST — the adapter is where the protocol lives, and the URL it builds is the adapter's own. (4) THE ADAPTER SEAM IS UNCHANGED: `ask(call: ToolCall, credential: Secret) -> ProviderAnswer`. That is deliberate and it is what makes the field policy structural — the `ToolCall` is the only thing an adapter has to build a body from, so a field the policy withholds is a request that cannot exist. If you need to send more than the indicator, add the field to `ToolCall`, add it to `helena.disclosure.SENDABLE_FIELDS` (a test asserts the two sets are equal), and permit it in the file — in that order, or the tool refuses every call. (5) A CACHE HIT RECORDS NO DISCLOSURE AND THE COUNTS RECONCILE: `len(disclosures.to_channel(PROVIDER_LOOKUP)) == budget.live_queries_spent`. If you add a path that reaches a provider, it charges the live query AND records the row, or that assertion in tests/test_tools.py fails — which is the intended way to find out. (6) THE LEDGER IS IN MEMORY AND NOTHING STORES IT. `Disclosures.rows` is the column task 43 owes, beside `RunBudget.cost`; until then the record dies with the process, and the README and ADR-0027 §6 both say so. Do not 'fix' this with a table without reading ADR-0027 §6 first — it is the same deferral `Cost` has. (7) `config/policy.toml` NOW HAS THREE TABLES AND THREE LOADERS. A bare key appended at the foot of that file lands inside `[rate_limits]`; version keys go at the top. If you add a fourth table, add its key set to `helena.policy` beside the other three or the existing loaders will refuse the file.
